clinician.trajectory_summary: A 75-year-old woman with chronic renal insufficiency presented with vomiting, diarrhea, confusion, epigastric pain, and weight loss. Laboratory studies revealed severe electrolyte depletion (hyponatremia 124 mmol/L, hypokalemia 3.1 mmol/L) and acute renal failure (creatinine 318.24 μmol/L, BUN 188 mg/dl) secondary to severe dehydration from secretory diarrhea. Colonoscopy identified a giant rectal polyp (8-9 cm, occupying 3/4 of luminal circumference). Biopsy confirmed villous adenoma with focal high-grade dysplasia. Following surgical resection of the tumor, the patient experienced persistent normalization of serological parameters and full recovery of renal function. At 10-month follow-up, she remained in good condition with regular GI function and no electrolyte disturbances or renal insufficiency.
